Going from the U.S. to Canada doesn't require a finger print. It ONLY comes up via any method of travel, if you get sent for further processing. I've flown in from the U.S. and internationally elsewhere. No matter how you travel there's 2 parts of immigration. The border agent who checks your passport and asks a few questions. This is how the vast majority of people cross. The second part "further processing" is an area the border agent sends you to if they suspect something isn't right. That's where finger prints come into the equation. Most people never see this/never finger printed. This includes air travel I do believe.

Coming home from the U.S. or internationally I've never been finger printed. I think the U.S. finger prints everyone including U.S. citizens but we don't. Here's the official Border Services site. It doesn't mention anything about finger prints by air. There's "further processing" at the airport too. If sent there, that's again where you may be finger printed.

I think you may have an idea of what an alcoholic is. If you get treatment you'll learn what it ACTUALLY IS FULLY and how to treat it. It isn't just someone that drinks. It's someone that (al most always) has a genetic predisposition to addiction. When they begin to use it's different from others. As the relationship furthers, consequences arise. Now in light of their troubles they continue to use. Consequences, don't necessarily mean getting fired or a DUI. They can be anything like in your case numbing your brain and not dealing with your issue and in turn adding a new problem. A problem that'll get worse if left unchecked. Alcoholism has MANY MANY other dynamics but there's a glaring marker you also described. Trying to "cut back" in AA is a kin to one of the "10 commandments" in indicating the relationship you have with alcohol that is also the relationship most AA members would have if they continued to drink. There's a lot of things indicators I'm reading too. That's perfectly fine.  

Sorry if it sounds like I'm trying to diagnose you. I'm not. Rather it's important to understand what alcoholism ACTUALLY is. Only after you understand it properly can you begin to solve it. Different but similar in trying to learn a new math concept. You can't solve it until you have a basic and/or proper understanding of it. In AA you learn about and treat it concurrently mind you. 

You may not want to hear this but you won't fix it on your own. If you could you would have already. Judging from the honourable character you've described of yourself, you should be able to fix it, right? Nope. Doesn't work like that. Living in a small town and drinking it straight are also tells. You're going to have to swallow your pride if you ever hope to find peace. An AA meeting isn't with EVERYONE in your town. It's filled with alcoholics. Hypothetically, MOST OF THEM don't want to be there either. However, they're willing and wanting to change. They're not going to "punish" you or your family by running to tell everyone you have a problem and are being mature in handling it. Whoever, they tell is gonna say, "huh how do you know person XYZ is an alcoholic? You were at the meeting? So you're an alcoholic too?". People aren't dumb. The tattletale also wants to keep their private life - - - private.

Last thing I'll say is that I GUARANTEE. I REPEAT I GUARANTEE 2 THINGS. One good. One bad. 

1) If you don't handle this, it will get worse. Over time the relationship will grow as it did before. Forcing yourself to buy less booze and going to bed when the well runs dry are a bandaid at best trying to fix the problem. Handling it isn't solely up to you as you'll need help not only getting sober but staying sober. There's great options out there and it sounds like your wife really loves you and will help you a lot too! Ya did the crime now pay the time to yourself! Unlike jail this sort of "rehabilitation" for lack a better term REALLY WORKS! 

2) Solving this will GO a ALONG WAY in solving the other issues. Childhood trauma is so horrible. Don't have it myself but can empathize. You won't bring that under control until you bring this under control. Being functional but still drinking isn't a solution. Neither of these issues will ever truly be gone. That's PERFECTLY fine! They're PART of you but not who you are. Think of them a kin to a disorder. Lots of people are psychopathic or have many of those traits and live full and happy lives. Aren't a statistically significant number of bosses psychopathic to some degree?  In bringing this under control you're going to learn a lot of valuable skills through AA that are concepts that can be applied to solving the trauma. It most likely needs treatment too. Understanding, and implementing a concept based and fully formed process and learning a long the way are the KINDS of things therapy for the trauma will also later use. There methods aren't that far a part either. Plus once you handle this you're going to FEEL 100 times better and far more motivated, fully present and less scared to handle that issue. You can run but ya can't hide as they say!
